official.application_cycle: 2027 NSF GRFP competition (solicitation NSF 26-526; deadlines fall October 2026)
official.status_note: The 2027 Notice of Funding Opportunity (NSF 26-526) is published; the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov is open and all deadlines for the 2027 competition fall between October 16 and October 23, 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: $16,000 cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution covers ALL tuition and mandatory fees (no cost to student).
official.funding_period: per year (stipend to the fellow, for each of three years)
benefits: Five-year award with three years of financial support: $37,000 stipend plus $16,000 cost of education paid to the institution for each year of funding support ($53,000 each year for three years over a five-year period).
COE payment covers all tuition and mandatory fees (no cost to student).
Access to supplemental funding to sustain research while on medical leave.
Access to professional development opportunities and the NSF GRFP community.
The Fellowship is portable and can be transferred to a different institution of higher education; fellows can transfer after completion of the first Fellowship year.
eligibility: Must, at the time of submission, be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or a permanent resident ("green-card" holder).
Must intend to enroll or be enrolled full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM.
Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship, and must have declined any previously offered fellowship by the deadline (if applicable).

Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program (Level 1: final-year undergraduate or bachelor's holder with no graduate enrollment; Level 2: joint bachelor's-master's student in final undergraduate or first graduate year, or first-year graduate student in their first graduate degree program).
Must not be a current NSF employee.

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.

Individuals who have earned a master's, doctoral, or terminal degree in any field, or who will be enrolled in a practice-oriented professional degree program (e.g., MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, DDS) at any time during the fellowship, or who plan a joint science-professional degree program, are not eligible.
An eligible applicant may submit only one application per annual competition.
requirements: Prepare and submit the application in the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov; a Research.gov account is required and the module usually opens in July or August.
Provide accurate personal information: full legal name, mailing and permanent address, date of birth, high school location, and demographic information.

Select a level (Level 1 undergraduate or Level 2 graduate) and list all degree-granting undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, with enrollment status, enrollment dates, and degree conferred, plus significant academic honors, fellowships, scholarships, publications and presentations.
Select the Major Field of Study most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program and research plan; the Major Field of Study determines the application deadline and the reviewers.

Enter three reference writer names, organizational affiliations, and email addresses, ranked in order of preference; family members cannot be reference writers; two reference letters must be received by NSF by 8:00 p.m. ET on the reference letter date.

Statements must be PDF only, with required Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts headings: Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement (maximum three pages) and Graduate Research Plan Statement (maximum two pages).

Use standard 8.5" x 11" pages with 1" margins (no header, footer, name, or page number) and accepted fonts (Arial, Courier New, or Palatino Linotype 10-point or larger; Times New Roman or Computer Modern 11-point or larger); page limits include all references, citations, charts, figures, images, and publication lists.
Applications are automatically checked by the GRFP Application Module for compliance with format requirements; documents that are not compliant will not be accepted by the module.
documents: Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement (maximum three pages, PDF only).
Graduate Research Plan Statement (maximum two pages, PDF only).
Graduate transcripts, if applicable; these may be unofficial if the institution does not provide official transcripts for first-year, first-academic-term graduate students.
Two reference letters must be received by NSF (the module allows requests for up to five; if more than three are received, the top three are considered).
Completed application package submitted in the GRFP Application Module.
selection_criteria: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers, and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure reviewers have no conflicts of interest.
Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant.

Reviewers evaluate each application according to the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (the potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (the potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes).

Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, and persist and overcome challenges, plus demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards.

Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure.
coverage: $37,000 stipend paid to the fellow for each of the three years of support.
$16,000 cost-of-education (COE) allowance provided to the institution of higher education in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each Fellow using the support in a fellowship year.
$53,000 each year for three years over a five-year period.
Access to supplemental funding to sustain research while on medical leave.
application_method: Create a Research.gov account and access the GRFP Application Module (usually opens in July or August).
Enter personal information and select Level 1 or Level 2.
Enter all degree-granting institutions attended, enrollment details, honors, fellowships, scholarships, publications and presentations.
Upload official undergraduate transcripts in PDF (and graduate transcripts where applicable).
Select the Major Field of Study; this fixes your deadline and reviewer panel.
Request up to five reference letters and rank them; two letters must be received by NSF by 8:00 p.m. ET on the reference letter date (October 16, 2026).
Upload the Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement (three pages maximum) and the Graduate Research Plan Statement (two pages maximum) as PDFs.
Submit the completed application package in the GRFP Application Module by 8:00 p.m. ET on your field's deadline; only module submissions are accepted.
official.application_route: Apply online through the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov; emailed or mailed applications are not accepted.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, or permanent residents ("green-card" holders) at the time of submission; foreign nationals on student visas or awaiting green cards are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: No - only U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and permanent residents are eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Must pursue a research-based master's or doctoral degree in an NSF-supported STEM field at a nonprofit U.S. institution; practice-oriented professional degree programs (medical, dental, law, public health, MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, DDS) and joint science-professional degree programs are excluded at any time during the fellowship.
official.research_requirement: A Graduate Research Plan Statement presents an original research topic to be pursued in graduate school, including the research idea and proposed approach, resources needed, potential to advance knowledge (Intellectual Merit), and potential to benefit society (Broader Impacts).
official.duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
official.description: The NSF GRFP recognizes and supports outstanding graduate students in NSF-supported STEM disciplines pursuing full-time research-based master's and doctoral degrees at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period: a $37,000 annual stipend plus a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees.
official.program_type: Government fellowship (NSF, Directorate for STEM Education)

verification.notes: Amounts ($37,000 stipend plus $16,000 cost-of-education per year, $53,000 per year for three years over a five-year period), tuition-and-fees coverage, and the October 2026 deadline schedule were taken directly from NSF's GRFP pages and the NSF 26-526 solicitation summary; NSF does not publish an English-language proficiency requirement or a travel allowance for this program.

applicant_utility.summary: The GRFP covers your full tuition and mandatory fees through a $16,000 cost-of-education allowance to your institution and pays you a $37,000 annual stipend for each of three funded years inside a five-year window, so you must line up funding for the two unfunded years. Your chosen Major Field of Study sets your deadline, which ranges from October 19 to October 23, 2026, and all three reference writers must be lined up early because letters close on October 16, 2026. Eligibility hinges on being a U.S. citizen, national, or permanent resident who has completed less than one academic year in a graduate program, so final-year undergraduates, joint bachelor's-master's students, and first-year graduate students are the core applicant pool. Applications go only through the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov, and the module automatically rejects documents that break NSF's strict formatting rules.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year undergraduates, bachelor's holders with no prior graduate enrollment, and first-year research-based STEM graduate students who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and want five years of funding freedom with no service obligation.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your citizenship, national, or permanent-resident status as of the submission date before anything else.
Pick your Major Field of Study early - it determines both your deadline (October 19-23, 2026) and which reviewer panel reads you.
Ask three reference writers by early September and confirm each received the NSF email request; two letters must land by 8:00 p.m. ET on October 16, 2026.
Request official undergraduate transcripts in PDF now, plus graduate transcripts if you have any (unofficial is allowed for first-term graduate students).
Format both statements to NSF's rules exactly: 3-page personal statement and 2-page research plan, PDF only, 1-inch margins, approved fonts, and no text inside the margins.
Track application status in the GRFP Application Module rather than by email.
common_rejection_risks: Choosing a Major Field of Study whose deadline you cannot realistically meet - the field you pick, not the university, sets your due date.
Exceeding the page limits or breaking the font, margin, or PDF formatting rules - the module screens these automatically and non-compliant documents are not accepted.
Missing reference letters: with letters due three days before the earliest application deadline, a single silent recommender can sink an otherwise complete file.
Applying after completing more than one academic year in a graduate degree program, or after earning any master's or terminal degree, which permanently removes eligibility.
Proposing a professional or joint professional-PhD pathway (MD/PhD, JD/PhD, MBA and similar), which is excluded at any point during the fellowship.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The $16,000 allowance covers tuition and mandatory fees only, and the $37,000 stipend is the fellow's living support - personal research equipment, conference travel, health insurance, relocation, and living costs above the stipend are not published as covered. Two of the five fellowship years carry no NSF support, so plan teaching, assistantship, or other funding for those years.
document_audit: Undergraduate transcripts must be official and PDF; graduate transcripts may only be unofficial if your institution does not issue official transcripts to first-year, first-term graduate students.
Family members are barred as reference writers - vet your three recommenders before you send the module requests.
The 3-page and 2-page statement limits count references, citations, charts, figures, images, and publication lists, so a long bibliography eats into your actual content.
Nothing is accepted by email or mail - an incomplete module submission is simply not submitted.
alerts: Reference letters close October 16, 2026, before the earliest application deadline, so requests should go out at least a month earlier.
Withdrawing after November 15, 2026 counts the attempt against the limited number of times you may apply.
You get only one application per annual competition, and enrolled graduate students can apply only once, in the first year of their first graduate program.
The fellowship is portable only after you complete the first fellowship year, so treat your initial institution choice as binding for year one.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Everything is assembled and submitted in the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov, with reference letters uploaded directly by writers; NSF notifies applicants of decisions after the review cycle.

official.deadline_note: The 2026 cycle ran from March 5, 2026 (applications opened) to April 30, 2026 (applications closed); notification of proposal decisions was due by August 31, 2026 and public announcement of new fellowship recipients by October 31, 2026. Google has not published dates for the next cycle; the application submission portal appears on the programme page when the application period begins.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle; the 2026 cycle ran March 5 - April 30, 2026 and dates for the next cycle have not been published.
official.status_note: Applications are currently closed for the 2026 cycle; the 2026 window ran March 5 to April 30, 2026, with proposal decisions notified by August 31, 2026 and recipients announced publicly by October 31, 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: United States: US $85K per year towards education costs (tuition and fees), living expenses, travel, and personal equipment (effective from 2025 for new recipients).
benefits: United States and Canada: up to 2-year Fellowship of US $85K per year towards education costs (tuition and fees), living expenses, travel, and personal equipment (effective from 2025 for new recipients).

Other regional awards include: Africa up to 3 years of US $15K; Australia and New Zealand 1 year of AUD $20K; East Asia 1 year of US $10K; Europe and the Middle East up to 2 years with a yearly bursary varying by country; India up to 4 years of US $50K (early-stage) or 1 year of US $10K (late-stage); Latin America up to 2 years of US $15K per year; Southeast Asia up to 3 years of US $10K per year or up to graduation, whichever is earlier.
Any monetary awards are paid directly to the Fellow's university for distribution, with no overhead assessed against them.
Fellowships begin at the start of the upcoming school year after award notification.
Fellowship recipients remain eligible for other Google scholarships.
Fellowship recipients do not become employees of Google, and the award does not increase the chances of a Google internship or job.
eligibility: Enrolled full-time in a PhD programme in computer science or an adjacent field at an accredited research institution that awards research degrees to PhD students.
Must be nominated by an eligible university during the application window; direct applications from students are not accepted.
Must remain enrolled full-time in the PhD programme for the duration of the Fellowship or forfeit the award.
United States and Canada: students must have completed graduate coursework in their PhD by the academic award year when the Fellowship begins.
Google employees, and their spouses, children, and members of their household, are not eligible.
Students already supported by a comparable industry award are not eligible (government or non-profit organization funding is exempt); past PhD Fellowship awardees are not eligible to apply again.
requirements: All students must be nominated by an eligible university during the application period; the university submits the application on the student's behalf through the portal that becomes available on the programme page when the application period begins.
Submit all materials in a single, flat (not portfolio) PDF file.
Submit a research/dissertation proposal of maximum 3 pages, excluding references.
Meet the region-specific student stage requirement (for the United States: completed graduate coursework by the academic award year).
Complete the region-specific written responses for Canada and the United States, East Asia and Latin America (350-word limit essays).
Research should align with Google AI Principles; incomplete proposals will not be considered.
documents: Student CV with links to website and publications (if available).
Research/dissertation proposal, maximum 3 pages, excluding references.
Transcripts of current and previous academic records.
Two to three letters of recommendation from those familiar with the nominee's work (at least one from the thesis advisor for current PhD students).

Cover sheet signed by the Department Chair confirming the student passes eligibility requirements (required for Africa, Europe, the Middle East, Canada, East Asia, the United States and Latin America).
Short (1-page) CV of the student's primary PhD advisor.

For Canada and the United States: two student essay responses of up to 350 words each - one on the desired impact of the research on the field and society, and one on leadership experience positively influencing others over time.
selection_criteria: Applications are evaluated on the strength of the research proposal, research impact, student academic achievements, and leadership potential.

Proposals are evaluated for innovative concepts relevant to Google's research areas, plus robustness and potential impact to the field, and should include the direction and plans for the work in addition to a description of the research being pursued.
In Canada and the United States, East Asia and Latin America, essay responses are evaluated in addition to application materials to determine an overall recommendation.
A nominee's status as a member of a historically marginalized group is not considered in the selection of award recipients.
Universities may nominate up to four eligible students in Canada and the United States.
coverage: US $85K per year towards education costs (tuition and fees), living expenses, travel, and personal equipment (United States and Canada, effective from 2025 for new recipients).
Coverage and amounts vary by region and are published per region on the programme page; award payments are made directly to the Fellow's university with no overhead assessed.
application_method: Contact your department or graduate school about the university's internal nomination process.
If nominated, the university submits your application on your behalf through the submission portal that appears on the programme page when the application period begins.
Upload a single flat (not portfolio) PDF containing the CV, research proposal, transcripts, letters of recommendation, department chair cover sheet, advisor CV, and any region-specific essays.
official.application_route: University-nomination only: your institution submits the application through Google's portal during the application window; direct student applications are not accepted.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - fellowships are offered worldwide across Africa, Australia, Canada, East Asia, Europe, India, Latin America, the Middle East, New Zealand, Southeast Asia and the United States, subject to region-specific criteria.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: PhD in computer science or an adjacent field at an accredited research institution that awards research degrees; proposals should align with Google's listed research areas (including machine learning, machine perception, NLP, HCI, privacy/safety/security, quantum computing, software engineering, systems and networking, health research, algorithms and optimization, and computer architecture).
official.research_requirement: A research/dissertation proposal of maximum 3 pages excluding references, evaluated for innovative concepts relevant to Google's research areas, robustness, potential impact, and alignment with Google AI Principles.
official.duration: United States: up to 2 years; duration varies by region from 1 year (Australia and New Zealand, East Asia) up to 4 years (India, early-stage students).
official.description: The Google PhD Fellowship Program was created to recognize outstanding graduate students doing exceptional and innovative research in areas relevant to computer science and related fields, supporting promising PhD candidates of all backgrounds who seek to influence the future of technology. Students must be nominated by their university and the details of each Fellowship vary by region.
official.program_type: Industry-sponsored doctoral fellowship awarded through university nomination
official.english_requirement: All application materials should be submitted in English.

verification.notes: Award amounts, coverage, documents, eligibility rules, review criteria and the 2026 cycle dates were taken from Google Research's official PhD Fellowship programme page and its FAQs; Google has not published the dates of the next application cycle, so no central deadline is recorded.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply to the Google PhD Fellowship yourself - your university must nominate you through an internal process, so the first move is asking your department or graduate school whether it nominates and by what internal cutoff. For the United States, the award is up to $85,000 per year for up to two years towards tuition and fees, living expenses, travel and personal equipment, paid to your university with no overhead. To be eligible in the U.S. you must have completed graduate coursework by the academic award year, which typically means applying after your first year. The 2026 cycle ran March 5 to April 30, 2026 and the next window has not been announced, so watch the programme page in early spring.
applicant_utility.best_fit: PhD students in computer science or adjacent fields who have finished coursework, work on topics aligned with Google's listed research areas, and attend a department that runs an internal nomination process.
application_readiness_checklist: Email your graduate program administrator well before spring to confirm your school nominates and to get its internal deadline.
Check that you have completed (or will complete) graduate coursework by the academic award year, the U.S.-specific stage requirement.
Distil your work into a 3-page proposal excluding references that names the research direction, not just what you have done so far.
Ask your thesis advisor for a one-page CV and a recommendation letter, and have the Department Chair sign the eligibility cover sheet.
Draft the two 350-word essays (research impact; leadership) required for U.S. applicants early - they carry real weight in the overall recommendation.
Assemble everything into one flat PDF before your university's internal deadline, since late submissions are not reviewed and extensions are not granted.
common_rejection_risks: Discovering your department does not nominate, or missing its internal cutoff, since direct student applications are not accepted at all.
Not having completed graduate coursework by the award year in the U.S. or Canada, which makes the nomination void even with a strong proposal.
Holding another comparable industry award, which disqualifies you even though government or non-profit funding does not.
Submitting an incomplete proposal or missing region-specific documents such as the department chair cover sheet or the advisor's one-page CV.
Applying late in the window, as late submissions are not reviewed and extensions are not granted.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: In the U.S. the $85,000 per year is directed towards tuition and fees, living expenses, travel and personal equipment rather than a guaranteed full-cost package, so anything the award does not reach locally - full tuition at high-fee institutions, dependents' costs, or relocation - remains on you. Awards are paid to your university for distribution, so confirm disbursement timing with your graduate office.
document_audit: Everything must go in as a single, flat PDF - portfolios or linked attachments break the submission.
The proposal limit is three pages excluding references, and the two U.S. essays are capped at 350 words each; content beyond the caps is simply not considered.
The cover sheet must be signed by the Department Chair confirming eligibility - chase this signature before your university's internal deadline.
Your advisor must supply a separate one-page CV in addition to the recommendation letter, a requirement applicants routinely overlook.
U.S. universities may nominate at most four students, so internal competition can be tighter than the global numbers suggest.
alerts: Applications are currently closed; the next cycle is expected to open around spring 2027 following the March-April 2026 pattern, but no dates have been published.
You must stay enrolled full-time for the duration of the Fellowship or forfeit the award.
Google employees and their households are ineligible, and past awardees cannot reapply.
Fellowship IP restrictions apply only if you later complete a Google internship; the award itself creates no IP obligations and does not improve your internship or job prospects.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Your university's representative submits the nomination package through Google's portal, which becomes available on the programme page when the application period opens.
